wv_coliseum_the.blurb: The Coliseum is the hard-sport wall at Summersville Lake, a short trail walk from the climbers' lot in the state park near Summersville. All 14 routes are bolted single pitches, and every one starts at 5.12 or above, with the bulk in the 5.13s and 5.14s and a couple at the very top of the scale. The wall is steeply overhanging, and climbers describe the stone as clean, pale and very good quality, with flat edges, slopers and bigger holds on the steeper parts. It is a project-and-redpoint venue rather than a place to warm up, so most visitors pair it with easier walls elsewhere around the lake. Expect a quiet day compared with the lake's moderate crags.

wv_mad_butcher_block.blurb: Mad Butcher Block is a compact bouldering spot in the Roadside zone of Coopers Rock State Forest, in northern West Virginia. It holds 14 problems spread over the main block and a few small boulders nearby, including a short block just downhill. Grades run from V0 up to V4, with half of them at V3, so it suits climbers in the middle of the bouldering range. The namesake traverse across the main block is the best-known line. Holds can be fragile when damp, so it pays to wait for dry rock. To find it, follow the main trail through the corridors until the trail opens out and a chalked block stands on the hillside to your right.

wv_fayette_station_boulders.blurb: Fayette Station Boulders is a small riverside cluster on the floor of the New River Gorge, inside the national park. It holds 14 problems with a very wide spread: a few easy slabs and low-grade lines, a middle group around V3 to V5, and a handful of serious hard problems up to the double-digit V grades. The sandstone is good quality and dries quickly, which makes it a favourite for a short session between other stops along Fayette Station Road. It has some of the easiest access of any bouldering in the gorge. Fall through spring is the comfortable season, and a high river can put the lower blocks underwater, so check the gauge first.
wv_fayette_station_boulders.approach: From the boat ramp at the far end of the rafters' lot, a couple of minutes of scrambling over riverside talus downstream reaches the blocks.

wv_02_simpson_wall.blurb: Simpson Wall is the farthest downstream of the well-developed cliffs in the Bozoo area of southern West Virginia, a quiet sandstone band reached from the Shanklin's Ferry campground side. Its 14 climbs are mostly traditional lines, with three top-rope problems and one boulder problem. Grades are broad: a few easy classics in the 5.7 to 5.8 range, a solid middle at 5.9 and 5.10, and several routes from 5.11 into the 5.12s. A large cave sits under the main buttress. Bozoo is rarely crowded, and the foliage here throws a lot of summer shade. The directions to the base are fiddly, so bring GPS coordinates or an offline map.

wv_1_the_hole.blurb: The Hole is a small, steep sport crag in the Kaymoor section of the New River Gorge, with the shortest walk of any crag there. All 14 routes are bolted, and the grades sit in a narrow, demanding band: four at 5.12 and ten at 5.13. The sandstone is dramatically overhanging, so expect powerful roof moves, linkups and awkward clips rather than easy warm-ups. The cave is well sheltered from rain, but it tends to seep and feel humid, so it climbs better in cooler, drier conditions. Upper Kaymoor sits a short stroll to the climber's right, which makes it simple to add easier lines to a day here.
